stem: Lactic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)COOH}$, is the only monomer needed to form the polymer polylactic acid, PLA.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text:
Draw a short length of the PLA polymer chain, including a minimum of two monomer residues. The methyl groups may be written as $-\text{CH}_3$ but all other bonds should be shown fully displayed.

Label one repeat unit of polylactic acid on your diagram.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Give the name of the type of polymerisation involved in the formation of PLA and the name of the functional group that forms between the monomers.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Predict whether PLA is readily biodegradable. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The proton ($^1\text{H}$) NMR spectrum of $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)COOH}$ in $\text{CDCl}_3$ is shown in Fig. 8.1. The proton NMR chemical shift ranges are shown in Table 8.1.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

Fig. 8.1

Table 8.1

| environment of proton | example | chemical shift range $\delta/\text{ppm}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| alkane | $-\text{CH}_3$, $-\text{CH}_2-$, $>\text{CH}-$ | 0.9-1.7 |
| alkyl next to C=O | $\text{CH}_3-\text{C=O}$, $-\text{CH}_2-\text{C=O}$, $>\text{CH}-\text{C=O}$ | 2.2-3.0 |
| alkyl next to aromatic ring | $\text{CH}_3-\text{Ar}$, $-\text{CH}_2-\text{Ar}$, $>\text{CH}-\text{Ar}$ | 2.3-3.0 |
| alkyl next to electronegative atom | $\text{CH}_3-\text{O}$, $-\text{CH}_2-\text{O}$, $-\text{CH}_2-\text{Cl}$ | 3.2-4.0 |
| attached to alkene | $=\text{CHR}$ | 4.5-6.0 |
| attached to aromatic ring | $\text{H}-\text{Ar}$ | 6.0-9.0 |
| aldehyde | $\text{HCOR}$ | 9.3-10.5 |
| alcohol | $\text{ROH}$ | 0.5-6.0 |
| phenol | $\text{Ar-OH}$ | 4.5-7.0 |
| carboxylic acid | $\text{RCOOH}$ | 9.0-13.0 |

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Name the substance responsible for the peak at $\delta = 0.0$.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Explain why $\text{CDCl}_3$ is a better solvent than $\text{CHCl}_3$ for use in proton NMR.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: An impure sample of $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)COOH}$ contains pentan-3-one as the only contaminant. The mixture is analysed using gas/liquid chromatography. The pentan-3-one is found to have a longer retention time than the lactic acid.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by retention time.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest suitable substances, or types of substances, that could be used as the mobile and stationary phases.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Describe how the percentage composition of the mixture can be determined from the gas/liquid chromatogram.
